lines: Commits on track/p-erasure-phones (on d1756b3), not pushed, rebased or landed: 7201d4b feat(erasure): scrub national-form phones and re-scrub erased clients; 43765c6 docs(erasure): name re-scrub false matches and limit its pre-flight (doc only, release_manager/docs/client-erasure.md).

43765c6 answers review-45 (PASS with notes). M1: the doc names the non-phone shapes the re-scrub also replaces in free text: a 10-digit account number starting 6-9, a 91-prefixed 12-digit UTR, ten-digit paise and rupee amounts, five-digit ranges, and the national part of foreign numbers. Each example was checked against the real pattern. The account and UTR shapes are described without literal values (DEC-25). It adds a read-only SQL query that shows the free text of the rows a dry run names (one id list covers every table) and says --apply only follows an explicit maintainer decision to accept that scope.

L1: the pre-flight now counts only client.erased rows before a DEC-66 deploy time the maintainer fills in. The doc says the command itself has no date limit. It also says a production database going straight from v0.15.4 has never had the erase command and should not run the re-scrub (checked: 261d5e3 first appears in v0.16.0; v0.15.4 has no clientErasure.ts). L2: keep the --apply report with the release record. L5: the JSON rule says free-text values also lose a known phone's digits without the +. The stale status line now says the feature has been released from v0.16.0 and that production erasures are not recorded in the doc.

Verification for 43765c6: git diff --check is clean. No new runs were recorded. The code is unchanged, so the runs for 7201d4b stand: contracts 20261117T105721Z-955619, backend check 20261117T105742Z-959894 (102 files / 1209 tests), integration 20261117T105829Z-974051 (74 files / 592 tests), red controls R1-R5 20261117T105925Z-1037151, 20261117T105939Z-1044898, 20261117T105952Z-1051292, 20261117T110007Z-1057950, 20261117T110021Z-1061832.

Unchanged from the first hand-off: rule 11 (no schema, API or contract change), the runtime steps (local dry run on a disposable DB; production only as pre-flight, then dry run, then reading the named rows, then an explicit decision, then --apply), and the doubtful items (hyphen separator, the pattern's false matches, values with no letter or space left as they are, nothing run on a real DB or VPS). DEC-66 status and plans/admin-improvements.md are the operator's.
Commit: 7201d4b feat(erasure): scrub national-form phones and re-scrub erased clients (one commit on track/p-erasure-phones, on d1756b3). Not pushed, rebased or landed.

WHAT 1, future erasures (DEC-66): erasureContacts.ts now matches a +91 phone in every national form through one pattern from the new erasurePhoneForms.ts: 10 digits, 5+5 split by one space or hyphen or unsplit, alone or after +91/91/0 with or without one space or hyphen, digit-bounded. Text pass: all forms. JSON: stored +91 form in every string as before; national forms only in string values with a letter or whitespace. Digit-only strings and JSON numbers are never touched. Same transaction, same 'tombstone' replacement. Known phones are the existing set (live phone, contact-history phones, linked application phone, minus phones another user holds).

WHAT 2, re-scrub: src/scripts/rescrubErasedPhones.ts (npm run erasure:rescrub-phones / :dev) -> domain/admin/erasedPhoneRescrub.ts + repositories/erasedClientRepository.ts. The original numbers cannot be recovered (DEC-29 overwrote users, history and applications; no phone hash is kept; only last-4 endings survive in audit metadata). So it uses a pattern for Indian mobiles ([6-9] then 9 digits, same separators and prefixes, no letter/digit/_/- right before, no letter/digit/_ right after, so a UUID's last group is not cut), only in free-text values, only in the erased clients' own rows. Clients are users with a client.erased audit row. Rows are the erasure's CLIENT_SCRUB_TARGETS plus receipts, with applications = users.application_id plus applications carrying the erased placeholder email. A contact-history reason_detail that mentions a mobile is nulled through the 069 path (markErasing).

Re-scrub behaviour: a dry run by default (one transaction, rolled back); --apply commits; prints mode, erasedClients, per-table counts and changed row ids (no values). It refuses NODE_ENV=production without --allow-production, in both modes, and refuses unknown flags (exit 2, nothing read). Idempotent. No audit row; the printed report is the record. Never run on any real database.

Supporting changes: scrubTarget now returns changed ids instead of a count (callers ignored the count); listOwnedEntities takes Pick<ErasureSubject,'id'>. Doc: release_manager/docs/client-erasure.md (scrub rules, the Q-46 paragraph, a new re-scrub section with a read-only pre-flight SQL and the production run, tests).

Rule 11: no migration and no schema change. No API, contract or response-shape change; released apps are unaffected. Writes only text inside the erased client's own rows (more phone forms replaced), the same class of write DEC-29 already approved. The previous release runs unchanged. An erasure made while rolled back misses national forms, and the re-scrub can cover it after the roll-forward. The re-scrub is maintainer-run, dry-run first and idempotent.

Tests: test/integration/clientErasurePhones.integration.test.ts has 3 tests. (1) In a G2 erasure, a decline reason, audit metadata note and support text with the current and former phones in national forms read tombstone. (2) Digit-only amountPaise/referenceId and a JSON number with the same digits are unchanged. (3) Re-scrub over a G2 and a G3 erased client plus a bystander: the dry run leaves the DB byte-identical and names exactly the 6 planted rows; apply changes them and not the bystander's; a second apply reports nothing and leaves the DB byte-identical. Unit tests: erasureContacts.test.ts (+2 cases), new src/scripts/rescrubErasedPhones.test.ts (3).

Red controls (all exit 1, each file restored and cmp-identical): R1 20261117T105925Z-1037151, erasureContacts.ts reverted to base, test 1 fails (3 readable copies). R2 20261117T105939Z-1044898, free-text guard removed, test 2 fails (amountPaise -> tombstone). R3 20261117T105952Z-1051292, dry run commits, test 3 fails at the snapshot after the dry run. R4 20261117T110007Z-1057950, replacement keeps the number, test 3 fails at the second-apply assertion. R5 20261117T110021Z-1061832, production refusal disabled, unit test fails.

Green runs on 7201d4b, clean tree, Node 24 container: contracts npm ci + build 20261117T105721Z-955619. Backend npm ci + npm run check 20261117T105742Z-959894: 102 files / 1209 tests, unit coverage lines 81.68%. Full integration suite, coverage off, 20261117T105829Z-974051: 74 files / 592 tests. Frontend not touched, not run.

Runtime steps for the coordinator (none were run here). Local: point DATABASE_URL at a disposable local DB and run `npm run erasure:rescrub-phones:dev`; expect a JSON report with mode dry_run and erasedClients 0 on a DB with no erasures. Erase a seeded local client whose receipt or support text holds '98765 43210'; the row then reads 'tombstone'. Production (maintainer only): run the doc's pre-flight SQL first. If it is above 0, run `run --rm --no-deps migrate node dist/scripts/rescrubErasedPhones.js --allow-production` through the stack's compose wrapper, review the row ids, then add --apply.

Doubtful / for review: (a) I accept a hyphen as a separator as well as the space the brief listed, and this is documented. (b) The re-scrub cannot tell the client's own number from any other mobile in those rows, such as a relative's or a support line, and replaces them all. A receipt naming the erased id and also other clients counts as the client's, as in the erasure. (c) A value with no letter or space, such as '98765-43210' alone, is left, which is the literal reading of DEC-66. (d) Text columns now replace spaced forms too, and history reasons are nulled more often. (e) Not verified: any real DB, a VPS, or the compose invocation on a stack (STATIC). (f) The DEC-66 status in tally and plans/admin-improvements.md were not touched; they are the operator's.
